To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

drivers are distracted by in-car information systems that do not adapt their speech to the driving environment, and that drivers perform as well in the secondary task when in-car information systems intelligently interrupt their speech and resume it as they do in control conditions.

(1) the proposed system is able to adapt the delivery of information in real-time to the driving situation; (2) drivers are distracted when they are not allowed to adapt their driving to the delivery of information; (3) drivers are not distracted when they are allowed to adapt their attention to the driving task by the system's intelligent adaptation; and (4) drivers perform better in a secondary task when they can adapt their attention to driving by the intelligent system than in the case when the system

a system that is able to interrupt its delivery of information when the driving task demands more attention from the drivers and resume its delivery when the driving task becomes less demanding is able to improve the performance of the drivers on both the primary and the secondary tasks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
designing a speech output delivery mechanism for in-car information systems that can adapt to the situation of the driver, and the results indicate a potential benefit for drivers.
designing and evaluating a situationally-aware in-vehicle information system that is able to adapt its speech delivery to the driving environment.
the design of an in-vehicle system that can deliver information in a way that does not cause significant distraction to the driver.

the proposed system can significantly reduce driver distraction by intelligently delivering information in a driving context, but more research is needed to determine whether such systems can be used in real driving environments and to what extent.
the system is able to reduce driver distraction by intelligently interrupting the speech when the driving task is more demanding and resuming it otherwise.
our system is able to reduce driver distraction by adapting to the driving situation, while a system that does not do so is unable to do so.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated the benefits of situationally-aware speech generation in the driving domain.
the system can adapt its output to a situationally aware incremental speech output generation.
we have designed and tested a system that uses situationally-aware incremental speech generation to reduce distraction in a driving environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the design of in-car speech output systems should be informed by the driving environment.

in-car speech-based systems should be designed to be sensitive to the driving environment, and that such sensitivity can be provided by an incremental speech output generation system that uses the driving environment to decide when to interrupt and when to resume its delivery.

a system which can adapt to the driving conditions can be more helpful than one which does not. We also demonstrate that the system can be designed to work in real time, which is a requirement for any practical implementation.
